A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BDetCLIP, with matching core methodology and figures despite retitling and restructuring. All 21 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original backdoor-detection experiments, inference-time measurements, prompt ablations, and supplementary evaluations in Tables 1–18.

after.justification: v3 reports original detection experiments, threshold evaluations, defense comparisons, and robustness results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core contrastive-prompt statistic remains unchanged. Threshold calibration changes from the minimum clean-validation score in v2 Appendix B to an 85th-percentile selection after descending ranking in v3 Section 4.3. The new BadEncoder application also uses reversed contrast differences. These are limited procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: v3 adds STL-10 evaluation with BadEncoder, an ImageNet–Caltech-101 open-set scenario, WaNet warping and TrojVQA dual-key attacks, semantically meaningful Hello Kitty triggers, and multi-target attacks. The ImageNetV2 evaluation is removed. BadCLIP-1 and BadCLIP-2 rename attacks already evaluated in v2; ISSBA was also already present.

E2.justification: v3 adds ASR comparisons against CleanCLIP, CleanerCLIP, PAR, and RoCLIP in Tables 11–12, plus a qualitative negative result for SAFECLIP in Appendix C. STRIP, SCALE-UP, and TeCo remain core comparators, but STRIP and TeCo are removed from the corresponding Ant/Basketball comparisons retained in v3 Table 22.

E3.justification: v3 introduces calibration sampling rates of 1%, 0.5%, and 0.1%, accuracy/recall/F1 evaluation, and an ASR protocol using entirely backdoored test inputs with detected samples discarded. The stated target changes from Ant to Banana in the ViT comparison and prompt-sensitivity experiments. These are reported protocol revisions and additions, without establishing that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds calibration-sample sensitivity, prompt-count/threshold analysis, and open-set, semantic-trigger, and multi-target robustness tests. It expands prompt generators from two to eight open-source models and extends the benign-prompt sweep to seven prompts. Conversely, v2 Table 9's prompt-component ablation and its BadCLIP-plus-CleanCLIP detection analysis are removed.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. v3 adds uncertainty reporting for thresholded performance and ASR in Tables 8–12, explicitly describes ten random resamplings in Appendix C, and calculates threshold means and variances from ten resamplings in Appendix D.7. This introduces substantial calibration-variability reporting, not evidence of ten independently trained models.

E6.justification: Reported BDetCLIP AUROCs change substantially: Banana/BadNet changes from 0.930 to 0.972 in Table 1, the CC3M-pretraining average from 0.930 to 0.959 in Table 5, and Liang's BadCLIP from 0.694 to 0.900. Numerous calibration, ASR, and robustness results are added, while removed analyses lose their results. Changed targets and v2's unspecified default prompt count prevent interpreting every revision as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 8 mathematically defines the threshold as a minimum over clean-validation scores; v3 replaces this with a non-equivalent percentile rule. The other loss, probability, detection-objective, and contrastive-score equations are retained apart from presentation and numbering. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: pioneering efficient test-time CLIP backdoor detection, using sensitivity to contrastive class prompts, and outperforming existing detection methods in effectiveness and efficiency.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes difficulty detecting Liang's BadCLIP and compatibility with CleanCLIP; v3 instead argues for superior standalone defense through its new ASR comparisons. It adds calibration-stability and open-set-transfer interpretations, softens the prompt-length sensitivity description under changed targets, and proposes semantics-adaptive triggers and prompt-quality assessment as future work.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses the default of seven benign prompts, optimizer and learning-rate schedules, five fine-tuning epochs, and 64 pretraining epochs with batch size 128. Appendix B adds attack-specific encoders and weight sources. The abstract also announces a public BDetCLIP repository, absent from v2. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without proving that previously used training settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting TrojVQA, PAR, STL-10, additional language models, and prompt alignment, and corrects the text-to-image example's citation to Ramesh et al. It removes the discussion of several CLIP-alignment variants and other backdoor-learning paradigms. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and substantially reorganized. Background discussion is shortened, experimental descriptions are rewritten, prompt analysis joins Section 4.2, threshold selection moves into Section 4.3, and limitations and future work become main-text sections. Appendices A–F become A–D with numbered experimental subsections; author affiliations and publication text also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, resizes and relocates the four retained figures, and restructures Table 1 around attack families. It introduces calibration and defense tables, reorganizes appendix displays, and separates the earlier combined language-model timing/detection table. These are substantial visual changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical assessment through threshold-sensitivity experiments with operating-point metrics and uncertainty, broader threat tests, and fuller reproducibility documentation. These gains are tempered by removal of the direct prompt-component ablation and ImageNetV2 evaluation, and a new reporting inconsistency: Table 1 gives TeCo an average of 0.934 although its six entries average approximately 0.834. The net improvement is positive but limited.
